title: Distilling Bidirectional Embedding Teachers into Streaming-Compatible Causal Students

contributions.purpose: Provide streaming-compatible text embeddings (KV-cache reusable) without giving up the quality of bidirectional attention.
contributions.mechanism: A teacher-student distillation framework that trains a bidirectional teacher with GG-SM (Gradient-Guided Soft Masking) and distills it into a causal student by combining InfoNCE contrastive loss with MSE distillation loss.
contributions.evaluation: The distilled student achieves 68.1% gap-closure relative to the teacher on MTEB and enables 4.1x streaming speedup via KV-cache reuse.
contributions.source_quote: We introduce a teacher-student distillation framework that enables streaming-compatible text embeddings while preserving bidirectional embedding quality, combining InfoNCE contrastive loss with MSE distillation from a GG-SM-trained bidirectional teacher.

contributions.purpose: Quantify how much bidirectional embedding quality the causal student retains and its efficiency advantage over inference-time workarounds.
contributions.mechanism: Benchmarking the distilled student against the bidirectional teacher and Echo embeddings on an MTEB slice with latency measurements.
contributions.evaluation: 68.1% gap-closure on MTEB-slice (0.623 vs 0.645), outperforming Echo embeddings by 2.0 percentage points while enabling 4.1x mean latency speedup through KV-cache streaming.
contributions.source_quote: The distilled student achieves 68.1% gap-closure relative to the bidirectional teacher on MTEB-slice (0.623 vs 0.645), outperforming Echo embeddings by 2.0 percentage points while enabling 4.1x mean latency speedup through KV-cache streaming.

contributions.purpose: Characterize which embedding task types benefit from cross-attention-architecture distillation.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis of task-type variation in distillation effectiveness across MTEB task categories.
contributions.evaluation: Strong transfer for classification (1.03x) and clustering (0.80x) but limited transfer for pair classification (0.30x), suggesting embedding-level distillation primarily captures holistic semantic structure.

self_declared_provenance.quote: A bidirectional teacher is first trained using GG-SM progressive soft masking (Yuan et al., 2026) for stable causal-to-bidirectional transition.
Our work differs by distilling across attention architectures—from bidirectional teacher to causal student—to enable streaming compatibility while preserving embedding quality.

notes: Abstract reports the surprising finding that the student outperforms all baselines on long-context retrieval. Student does not match teacher quality (68.1% gap-closure, 0.623 vs 0.645); C3 shows weak transfer for pair classification (0.30x).
